newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HEARTS WIN 4-0 AT EDINBURGH RIVALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HEARTS WIN 4-0 AT EDINBURGH RIVALS.

text.p: Hearts won 4-0 at Hibernian in Wednesday's Edinburgh derby while Dundee United routed Aberdeen by the same scoreline to go third in the Scottish premier division.

Two goals from recent signing Jim Hamilton and strikes from John Robertson and Colin Cameron gave Hearts their biggest ever premier division victory over their city rivals, playing their first match under new manager Jim Duffy.
Hibs had defender Andy Millen sent off after 38 minutes for his second bookable offence with the score at 1-0, and from then on never looked like pulling themselves back into the match.
Millen will be suspended for Saturday's home game against champions and league leaders Glasgow Rangers, who face Celtic in the traditional New Year match on Thursday.
Dundee United's victory over Aberdeen came courtesy of two headed goals from former Rangers and Coventry defender Steve Pressley and a goal apiece for striker Robbie Winters and Swede Kjell Olofsson.
Aberdeen, who slip to fourth, level on points with United, have now taken just two points from their last five games.
